name: Sidebar
summary: Floating side panel that holds the application's navigation.

a11y.apg: No APG pattern covers site navigation, and that absence is the decision: the practice adopted is native links inside a <nav>, natural Tab order, and aria-current="page" on the current item. A roving tabindex (the TreeView pattern) is deliberately NOT used — in a sidebar people expect Tab to walk the items one by one. The landmark comes from the element: <aside> is complementary and the <nav> is nested inside it, never around it. As a drawer it is the native popover, so Escape, click-outside and focus return come from the browser.
a11y.keyboardNote: Measured in a browser on 27/08/2026. Space was delivered and not declared — the items are real <button>s, so the platform gives Enter and Space. Escape is declared and inert here: it closes the drawer, and the bank mounts the expanded sidebar, where there is nothing to close.

props.name: items
props.description: The navigation, as data. One shape covers grouping and nesting: an item with `items` and no href is a group heading; with an href it is a parent that also has a sublist. Each item is {id, label, href?, icon?, badge?, onClick?, items?}. M-01: an item may carry render (a ReactElement, your router's link) instead of href — it receives the item's skin, the current-page state and the item's content.

props.name: variant
props.description: floating is the default and it is what this design system looks like: the panel detaches from the edges, takes the card radius and a border all the way around. flush is the ONE exception this system makes to that rule, and it is opt-in: the sidebar sits against the edges, takes the full height and is separated from the content by a single rule instead of a gap. That is what four shipping apps do — Cloudflare, Sophos, Claude's own app and HeroUI's dashboard were the ones measured. Aurea's own pages stay floating; flush is there for the applications that want it.

props.name: current
props.description: The id of the item you are on. It gets aria-current="page", which is also what the skin paints — one source for both, so they cannot drift apart.

props.name: collapsed
props.description: Icon rail. Labels stay in the DOM as screen-reader-only text, and the panel narrows to --sidebar-rail. In AppShell, a floating rail keeps its outer margins in the grid track; flush uses the token as the raw track width. Controlled by you: the sidebar never decides on its own when to collapse.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the <nav> that `items` renders. Two navigation landmarks with the same name fail axe, so name it when a page has more than one.

props.name: children
props.description: Escape hatch, not legacy: when the list comes from a router or a CMS, pass your own markup and the <nav> and its label are yours. Rendered after `items` when both are given.

notes: The sidebar is the only component allowed to be flush, and it is opt-in. Cards, dialogs and panels keep the floating surface the design system is built on — this exception was granted explicitly, for this component, and it does not generalise. Having the variant and using it are two different things: Aurea's own pages are floating throughout, and flush exists for the applications that want it.

The rows inside keep their 18px radius in BOTH variants. The concentric rule (child radius = parent radius - padding) is written as calc() against --radius-card, not against the panel's own radius, so a flush panel with radius 0 does not drag the rows to zero with it. That rule describes a CARD-shaped panel; a flush panel is a different case.
